title: Frobenius-equivariant closed right adjoint from the supported triangle
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ with algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$, and coefficients $\Lambda=E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $i_0:Z_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ be a closed immersion with complementary open $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$, with $X_0$ separated of finite type over $k_0$, and let $i,j$ be their geometric base changes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Suppose on the specified $D^b_c(-,\Lambda)$ categories the exact functors $i_*,i^*,J,j^*,Rj_*$ have adjunctions $i^*\dashv i_*\dashv J$, $j^*\dashv Rj_*$, invertible counits $i^*i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $j^*Rj_*\cong\mathrm{id}$, $j^*i_*=0$, and supported triangles $i_*JK\xrightarrow eK\xrightarrow uRj_*j^*K\to$, unique on morphisms with prescribed middle component. Use the canonical Frobenius comparisons for $i_*,i^*,j^*,Rj_*$, preserving the open unit, and the coherent pullback composition identifications [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The prescribed comparison $a:g_X^*i_*\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*g_Z^*$ for $i_*$ is the right-adjoint mate, for the given adjunction $i^*\dashv i_*$, of the inverse of the pullback-composition comparison $d:g_Z^*i^*\xrightarrow{\sim}i^*g_X^*$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. The adjunctions are exact adjunctions: their units and counits commute with the specified shift isomorphisms. The given coefficient comparisons identify the supported triangles and their adjunction maps, commute with the Frobenius comparisons for the four prescribed functors and shifts, and satisfy their stated tower coherences. A Weil structure is an isomorphism $g_T^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ for geometric Frobenius, as in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex].
There is a unique natural Frobenius comparison $g_Z^*J\cong Jg_X^*$ whose closed pushforward identifies the counits in these supported triangles. It is the right-adjoint mate of the prescribed comparison for $i_*$, is compatible with exact shifts and the given coefficient comparisons, and makes the adjunction Hom bijections Frobenius-equivariant. For every Weil complex $(K,\theta_K)$, the induced structure on $JK$ is the one obtained by applying $i^*$ to the unique isomorphism between the Frobenius-pulled supported triangle and the supported triangle of $K$. Both adjunction unit and counit and all three arrows of the supported triangle are equivariant, and this lift is functorial in morphisms of Weil complexes. The assertion is about equivariance of underlying distinguished triangles, and does not assert a triangulation of the category of Weil pairs.

proof.text: The exceptional counit normalization and counit naturality give the first square for an arbitrary arrow P(K) → L. For a Weil object K, its first component is an isomorphism, as a composite of a, iPush(b) and iPush(exceptional(theta)). Mathlib isoTriangleOfIso₁₂ yields a triangle isomorphism t₀ with that component and middle component theta. Any two maps from P(T_K) to T_L with equal middle components agree: precompose with t₀ inverse and use S.unique_middle, then cancel. For the third component, jp(openUnit_K) is inverse to the open counit by the triangle identity, hence jp(P(openUnit_K)) is invertible by dj naturality. Under jp ⊣ jPush, precomposition with P(openUnit_K) is therefore injective. The triangle second-square equation and S.openUnit identify the third component with the prescribed one. This proves existence, uniqueness and all triangle component clauses.
